title: Crediting Back the Unspent Balance of a Lapsed Micro Market Funding Lot
content:
Where a subsidy funding lot on an Unattended Micro Market Program agreement has run past the months it stays drawable, the balance left unspent in it is credited back to the client against the settlement invoice for the period.

A lot stays drawable for the months printed against the market format, counted from the day the funding cleared, so the lapsed funding is what was paid in before that many months back from the day the credit is worked out.

## The calculation

The unspent balance is the lapsed funding less the drawdowns set against it, never below nothing; the credit is that balance at the credit share, together with the closure relief and the lapse share of the settlement read over the settlement-reading window; and the whole is held to the ceiling on credits in one settlement period printed against the market format, measured against that same settlement.

The lapsed funding, the unspent balance, the balance taken at the credit share, the share of the settlement credited for the lapse, the figure those and the closure relief make when added, the ceiling on credits in one settlement period and the credit handed back are each rounded to the nearest cent as they are taken, a figure falling exactly on the half-cent going to the nearest even cent. The credit is recorded against no kiosk, since it hands back funding rather than answering kiosk time.

## The quantities

Everything drawn against the agreement is set against the lapsed funding. The settlement-reading window is the month to the day the credit is worked out. The credit share is the standing credit share of 95 per cent. No closure relief is credited. No share of the settlement is credited for the lapse.

## A lapsed lot worked through

*Hypothetical inputs.* The agreement has taken 30000.00 USD of subsidy funding in all, of which 18000.00 USD was paid in within the months the market format keeps a lot drawable. Everything drawn against the agreement totals 9000.00 USD. The settlement read over the month to the day the credit is worked out is 1920.00 USD, and the market format prints a ceiling on credits in one settlement period of 25 per cent of that settlement.

The lapsed funding is 12000.00 USD. All 9000.00 USD drawn against the agreement is set against it, leaving an unspent balance of 3000.00 USD. At the credit share of 95 per cent that balance gives 2850.00 USD; no closure relief and no lapse share of the settlement are added, so the figure stands at 2850.00 USD. The ceiling on credits in the period is 480.00 USD, being 25 per cent of 1920.00 USD, so the credit handed back is 480.00 USD.

*Hypothetical inputs, second case.* Where everything drawn against the agreement exceeds the lapsed funding, the unspent balance is nothing rather than a negative figure.
